subject: Post-call: Inference lab plan (Redwood vs hyperscalers) & latency/throughput metrics
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@helioanalytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Inference lab plan (Redwood vs hyperscalers) & latency/throughput metrics

Samir — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and a proposed lab plan so we can validate Redwood's latency/throughput story against Helio's current hyperscaler endpoints.

Key asks from Helio:
- Confirm p95/p99 latency at production token sizes (avg payload ~512 tokens, long tails to 2k).
- Peak tokens/sec under sustained load for 1k concurrent streams.
- Cold vs warmed KV cache impact.
- Consistency of output (quality parity) for a handful of prompt templates.

Proposed lab plan (attached spreadsheet):
1) Baseline: run Helio's current endpoint (A) and Hyperscaler B (billed setup) using Helio sample prompts. Measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and error rates over a 30-minute sustained ramp.
2) Redwood A/B: run Redwood default config vs Redwood aggressive batching + quantized model variant. Same workload.
3) Warm/cold cache sweep: 0, 10, 100, 1000 warm requests before measurement.
4) Deterministic quality checks: 25 seed prompts, compare top-3 outputs for major regressions.

Success criteria: 10–15% lower p95 or equivalent p95 with 20–30% lower tokens/sec cost. Clear SLA/latency advantage or specific tradeoff map (latency vs cost).

Actions & owners:
- Samir: confirm the Helio endpoints and a single test service account we can use (API keys) by EOD Thursday.
- Marissa: spin up the Redwood lab, prepare the test harness and synthetic load generator.
- Rafael: prepare quantized variants and expected perf profiles; share initial kernel/quantization notes.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-lab-plan.xlsx (test matrix), sample-prompts.txt (25 canonical prompts).

I'll schedule 60m on Monday for a dry-run if that works.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir@helioanalytics.com>

Date: 2026-06-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Inference lab plan (Redwood vs hyperscalers) & latency/throughput metrics

Vivek — appreciate the clear plan. We can provide two Helio-managed endpoints (prod-mirror and canary) and a service key for testing. I confirmed with infra: rate limits are 3k rps for the prod-mirror; canary is bursty. We'll send keys by EOD.

A couple of clarifications:
- For the 1k concurrent streams target, we usually measure at client stream concurrency rather than raw RPS; happy to align on the harness.
- Quality checks: we care about top-1 semantic parity for billing-relevant prompts (pricing, AML checks).

Monday dry-run works for our team — prefer 10:00 PT.

Samir
Director, POC Engineering
Helio Analytics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@helioanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Inference lab plan (Redwood vs hyperscalers) & latency/throughput metrics

Looping everyone into the test-harness details. Rafael and I sketched the runner:
- Harness: k6 + custom tokenizer shim to replicate Helio's client batching.
- Measurement windows: 5m warm, 30m steady-state for each config, 10m cool-down. We'll collect p50/p90/p95/p99, tail latency histograms, tokens/sec, and 5xx rates.
- Variants to run in parallel: Helio prod-mirror, Hyperscaler-B, Redwood-default, Redwood-quant (int8-ish).

Initial resource needs: two m5-large controllers to drive load + ephemeral GPU nodes for Redwood runs (we'll spin up g4dn-equivalent). Cost estimate in the sheet.

I've added a 'fail conditions' section in the spreadsheet: if p99 > 2s for >5% of requests or >1% error rate, we pause and inspect.

I'll take point on the k6 scripts and the Drive folder. Rafael, can you drop the quant notes into the same folder? Samir, once we receive the API keys we'll run a short connectivity check Friday.

- Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@helioanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-06-17T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Inference lab plan (Redwood vs hyperscalers) & latency/throughput metrics

Quick update from the runtime side after initial micro-benchmarks:
- Redwood-default (fp16) at seq=512: p95 ~ 320ms, p99 ~ 680ms (single-GPU, continuous batching, warm cache).
- Redwood-quant (int8-ish) early run: p95 ~ 260ms, p99 ~ 540ms but with slight variance on long sequences (2k tokens) — we have mitigation steps (hybrid attention kernels) in the attached notes.
- Tokens/sec observed (steady): default ~1.2k tokens/sec per GPU; quant ~1.6k tokens/sec per GPU. These numbers are single-node; we'll document multi-node scaling next.

I've uploaded a short results CSV and the kernel/quant notes to the Drive link in the sheet. Marissa — the k6 work sounds good; when you run the warm/cold sweep, tag the runs with cache_state=warm/ cold and batch_policy=aggressive/default.

Samir — if you can share the sample platform traces after your baseline run, we can side-by-side the histograms.

Rafael
Lead Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Inference lab plan (Redwood vs hyperscalers) & latency/throughput metrics

Great first pass — Rafael, these early numbers look promising and give us a clear hypothesis to validate in the 30m runs. Next steps:
- Marissa: run connectivity check with Helio keys Friday; if green, schedule the 4x steady-state runs next Tuesday (Helio endpoints + Hyperscaler-B + Redwood-default + Redwood-quant).
- Rafael: prepare a short runbook for interpreting p95/p99 vs tokens/sec tradeoffs (include when to claim latency advantage vs cost advantage).
- Samir: share baseline histograms when available; we will align on labeling conventions for the plots.

I'll confirm Monday 10:00 PT for the dry-run. Thanks everyone — I added the test plan to the HubSpot deal and flagged the task for engineering approval.

Vivek

Redwood Inference
